prompt to reach for when nobody remembers where things were.

## The prompt

```text
You are continuing work on vibey, a queue-based conductor for autonomous software delivery
(https://github.com/the-vibey-project/vibey). Assume you remember nothing; the repository is
the only truth. Your working directory is a clone of it.

1. Read the law before acting. Read CLAUDE.md in full: its non-negotiables bind you. Then
   skim src/vibey_tools/gh/docs/doctrines.md for Doctrines 8, 10 and 12 — the sovereign
   path is preferred (8.a), status is evidence-bounded (10.f), and unattended authority is
   bounded by a gate, never by judgement (12.d).
2. Establish where things stand, from evidence only:
   - `git fetch origin` and `git log --oneline -15 origin/develop` — the integration branch.
   - `gh pr list --state open` — work in flight; a draft PR is someone's live work, never
     yours to merge or rewrite.
   - `gh run list --branch develop --limit 30` — what is red on develop. If anything is,
     stop here and follow docs/continuation/keep-green.md first.
   - `gh issue list --state open --limit 50` and scripts/backlog_expectations.json — what is
     owed, and which issues are operator holds (never act on a hold).
   - docs/estimate.md — the living roadmap and the delivery forecast (Doctrine 11).
3. Pick the next item: the highest-priority open issue that is not a hold, is not already
   covered by an open PR, and that you can finish and prove. Say which you chose and why.
4. Deliver it the way this project delivers everything (ADR-0039, CDD): state the intent and
   acceptance criteria, write the failing test, implement, run the gates, review your own
   diff, repair. The gates are listed in CLAUDE.md under "Commands worth memorizing"; the
   per-layer 100% branch-coverage floors are not optional. Code lives in classes with an
   interface beside them (ADR-0016); domain/ stays pure (ADR-0017).
5. Land it only as a pull request into develop: a branch, Conventional Commits, a changelog
   fragment under changelog.d/ when the change reaches an installed user. Never push to
   develop or main, never use --no-verify or --admin, never merge or approve your own PR,
   never force-push a branch you did not create.
6. Report, with evidence: what you changed, the gate results with numbers, the PR link,
   and anything you declined to do and why. "Done" means the PR is green, not that you
   wrote code.

If the right action would be irreversible, would need a credential you were not given, or
would change a sub-doctrine, stop and say so: those belong to a person.
```
